body:
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT_OPENED: Orpheus (enterprise tenant) — elevated 5xx rates in eu-central region, health checks failing on a subset of dedicated pool hosts. Pager: @alicew, @junpark. Severity: Sev2 :rotating_light:
Alice W: on it. joining call now. can someone paste error slice?
Jun Park: seeing consistent 502/504 from the dedicated pool frontends to model workers since ~08:02 UTC. error rate ~18% for tenant traffic (rolling 5m). CPU on a few hosts spiked then OOM-killed pods.
Maria S: per metrics: KV cache miss rate jumped, request qps steady. latency tail up ~300ms -> 1.2s. Not seeing model-level regressions. looks infra-y.
SRE Lead (Raj): summary for execs: dedicated pool hosts for Orpheus in eu-central started OOMing; cause unclear. customer impact: errors and degraded latency; some requests being retried.
NetOps (Elena): noticed recent DNS updates for Orpheus VIPs at 07:55 UTC (internal change from customer network). TTL was low (30s) — might have caused churn with our LB. Investigating correlation.
Customer Eng (Tom): customer reported errors at 08:05 UTC. They are on the line, want timeline and mitigation. They asked for traffic isolation if needed.
Alice W: plan A = isolate tenant on warm spare capacity in eu-central2, canary shift 10% traffic then full reroute. Plan B = cross-region failover to eu-west if warm capacity not clean.
Jun Park: I can trigger warm spin-up: `redwoodctl pool scale --pool orpheus-eu-central-warm --replicas 8` and attach via routing policy. Will start now.
Jun Park: (after a minute) warm pool starting, provisioning GPUs. ETA ~6m for model container readiness. logs: `pod orpheus-warm-1: pulled, container starting`.
Oncall Bot: NOTE: On-call handover scheduled at 09:00 UTC in 58m. Current primary: @alicew, secondary: @junpark.
Maria S: prepping config for tenant-scoped rate-limits and KV cache warmpath. will push a conservative cache warm strategy to avoid thundering herd.
SRE Lead (Raj): @netops please hold any DNS changes on Orpheus domain while we stabilize. if customer NIC change needs to proceed, coordinate with Tom.
NetOps (Elena): ack. Pausing external DNS pushes. I'll also check bgp/edge logs for flaps.
Customer Eng (Tom): told customer we will attempt graceful reroute to spare capacity first. they requested explicit confirmation before any cross-region DNS change.
Leo K: adding a short-lived ACL to route only Orpheus tenant traffic into the warm pool: `lbctl route-mod --tenant orpheus --add-destination eu-central2:orpheus-warm --weight 100`
Jun Park: applied route-mod for 10% canary: `lbctl route-mod --tenant orpheus --set-weights eu-central:90,eu-central2:10`
Alice W: monitoring error rate after canary shift. pls watch 5xx rate, p99 latency, and model token error counts.
Maria S: cache warm jobs started on warm pool. hooking prefix caches for the most common 5 prompt families.
(Oncall Bot): DEPLOYMENT_EVENT: orpheus-warm pool scaled to 8 replicas — healthchecks passing (7/8).
Jun Park: 10% traffic to warm pool is clean so far (3m). error rate dropped for those sessions to 0.5%. overall tenant error rate moved from 18% -> 12%.
SRE Lead (Raj): good. bump canary to 30% in 5m increments if stable. coordinate with NetOps before any DNS-level changes.
NetOps (Elena): confirmed no external DNS ops pending. however internal VIP flapping observed — loadbalancer is marking some backends as UNREACHABLE briefly. I'm going to drain 2 hosts with high OOMs and mark them for analysis: `lbctl backend-drain --host orpheus-uf-03`
Jun Park: draining those hosts now. Pod recycle in progress.
Customer Eng (Tom): customer wants a conservative timeline: if warm pool fully stabilizes by +30m, they will not require cross-region failover.
Alice W: agree. next step: if after 20m overall error rate not below 4% we prepare DNS cutover plan to eu-west as fallback. Steps for DNS cutover: 1) set LB-level full traffic shift to eu-west via internal routing, 2) update external DNS A/ALIAS with 5s TTL, 3) validate end-to-end for 15m, 4) close loop with customer.
Maria S: prepping the DNS cutover playbook. adding verification steps: `curl -H "X-Tenant: orpheus" https://api.redwood.example/healthz` and compare model response signatures.
Jun Park: quick healthcheck script running, sample output:```
GET /healthz 200 OK
model_version: v2.3.1
latency_p50: 120ms
latency_p99: 540ms
```
SRE Lead (Raj): make sure we capture request ids for any failing calls to hand to model team and for customer logs. add `X-Request-ID` propagate.
NetOps (Elena): we observed some upstream retries from customer's CDN — they lowered keepalive settings recently. I'll ask them to revert temporarily while we stabilize. Tom, can you relay that?
Customer Eng (Tom): relayed. customer rolled back their CDN keepalive at 08:35 UTC. they reported a small improvement in connection reuse.
Jun Park: warming more; increasing canary to 60% now. applying: `lbctl route-mod --tenant orpheus --set-weights eu-central:40,eu-central2:60`
Alice W: traffic now mostly on warm pool. monitoring... overall 5xx now 2.1%. p99 latency 620ms. that's acceptable for now.
Oncall Bot: ALERT: Scheduled on-call handoff in 10m. please annotate runbook for next oncall.
SRE Lead (Raj): annotation done. runbook notes: cause candidate = ephemeral DNS churn + LB backend OOMs; mitigation = warm pool spin-up, host drain, cache warm, route shift. next steps = postmortem and host memory profiling.
NetOps (Elena): draining completed on 2 hosts; they no longer receive traffic. marking for postmortem.
Maria S: cache warm completed. verifying hit rates — increased cache hit from 12% -> 68% on warm pool.
Jun Park: running final checks for 30m window. no new OOMs on warm hosts.
Customer Eng (Tom): customer confirmed traffic looks normal from their side, error volume dropped to near-zero. they appreciate the quick action.
Alice W: leaving the channel for handoff to @junpark in 5. I will create a status note for the incident and start the RCA timeline doc.
Jun Park: taking over as primary. will keep monitoring and coordinate with Tom for any regressions.
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: severity downgraded to Sev3 at 08:52 UTC.
SRE Lead (Raj): Nice job team. postmortem owners: Jun (infra), Maria (cache), Elena (netops). I will schedule a 3-day follow-up to validate memory configs and LB behavior.
Customer Eng (Tom): setting up a customer-facing incident note and sending to Orpheus stakeholder. they'll want timeline and next steps.
Alice W: leaving brief notes: actions taken, mitigations, customer comms. follow-up: look at pod memory requests/limits and our eviction thresholds for dedicated pools.
Jun Park: will export logs and hand to infra team: `logs export --tenant orpheus --since 08:00 --until 09:00 --output s3://redwood-incident-exports/2587654321/`
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT_CLOSED: monitoring only. will reopen if new errors >5% in next 2h.
SRE Lead (Raj): closing notes: no cross-region DNS cutover needed thanks to warm pool. we'll still run a postmortem and tune LB/DNS interactions. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
